timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: We're rolling out AI features. Compliance still applies to AI?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: More than ever. And AI breaks the usual compliance assumptions.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Outputs are probabilistic, training data carries bias, models are opaque, and they keep evolving.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: EU AI Act, ISO 42001 for AI management systems, NIST AI RMF, ISO 23894.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What does the EU AI Act demand?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Risk-based classification, transparency obligations, and conformity assessments for high-risk AI.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What do I need to document?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Model purpose, capabilities, limitations, training data, and decisions that affect people.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: For high-risk decisions, yes. And audit trails of inputs and outputs.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do we keep AI from going rogue?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Content-safety guardrails and controls against misleading or harmful output.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Purview Compliance Manager has AI templates. Defender for Cloud Apps assesses AI app risk.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: M365 Copilot is ISO 42001 certified, and they publish Transparency Notes for every AI service.
